prompt: How does the benzene ring itself respond to a strong oxidizing agent such as KMnO4?

choices.text: It is inert, even though KMnO4 cleaves alkene carbon–carbon double bonds
Its double bonds are cleaved, as alkene double bonds are
choices.why: Despite its unsaturation, the benzene ring is inert to KMnO4.

choices.text: It is oxidized to a phenol
choices.why: The ring isn't attacked. KMnO4 oxidizes alkyl side chains, not the ring.

choices.text: It is oxidized to benzoic acid
choices.why: Benzene has no side chain to oxidize, and the ring itself is inert to KMnO4.

explanation: Despite its unsaturation, the benzene ring is inert to strong oxidizing agents such as KMnO4, which will cleave alkene carbon–carbon bonds (Section 8.8). The aromatic ring does, however, make its alkyl side chains reactive toward oxidation.

prompt: What is the product when butylbenzene is oxidized by aqueous KMnO4?

choices.text: Benzoic acid
4-Phenylbutanoic acid, with only the end carbon oxidized
choices.why: The side chain is attacked at the benzylic position and converted into a single carboxyl group, so the product is benzoic acid.

choices.text: Phenol
choices.why: The ring keeps a carbon substituent: the side chain becomes –CO2H, not –OH.

choices.text: No reaction, because KMnO4 doesn't affect aromatic compounds
choices.why: The ring is inert, but alkyl side chains react rapidly with oxidizing agents.

explanation: Alkyl side chains react rapidly with oxidizing agents and are converted into carboxyl groups, –CO2H. The net effect is conversion of an alkylbenzene into a benzoic acid, Ar–R → Ar–CO2H. Butylbenzene gives benzoic acid in 85% yield.

prompt: When butylbenzene is oxidized by aqueous KMnO4 to benzoic acid, how many of the four side-chain carbons remain attached to the ring in the product?
explanation: The whole butyl chain is converted into a single carboxyl group: Ar–R → Ar–CO2H. Only the benzylic carbon remains, as the carbon of –CO2H; the other three side-chain carbons are lost.

prompt: How is terephthalic acid, used to make polyester fibers, produced industrially?

choices.text: By oxidation of p-xylene with air and a Co(III) catalyst
By Friedel–Crafts acylation of benzene, then reduction
choices.why: Terephthalic acid is made by side-chain oxidation of p-xylene.

choices.text: By oxidation of o-xylene with aqueous KMnO4
choices.why: The starting material is p-xylene, and the industrial oxidant is air with a cobalt catalyst.

choices.text: By sulfonation of toluene followed by hydrolysis
choices.why: Terephthalic acid comes from oxidation of both methyl groups of p-xylene.

explanation: A side-chain oxidation is used industrially to make the terephthalic acid used in polyester fibers. About 118 million tons per year are produced worldwide by oxidation of p-xylene, using air as the oxidant and Co(III) salts as catalyst. Both methyl groups become –CO2H groups.

prompt: Approximately how many million tons of terephthalic acid are produced worldwide each year by oxidation of p-xylene?
explanation: Worldwide, approximately 118 million tons per year of terephthalic acid is produced by oxidation of p-xylene, using air as the oxidant and Co(III) salts as catalyst.

prompt: What does the mechanism of side-chain oxidation involve?

choices.text: Reaction of C–H bonds at the position next to the ring to form intermediate benzylic radicals
Electrophilic attack of KMnO4 on the ring to form a carbocation
choices.why: The ring is inert to KMnO4. The reaction starts at the benzylic C–H bonds.

choices.text: Reaction of the C–H bond at the end of the side chain, farthest from the ring
choices.why: Reaction occurs at the position next to the ring, the benzylic position.

choices.text: Nucleophilic substitution of a ring hydrogen by hydroxide
choices.why: Side-chain oxidation involves benzylic C–H bonds and benzylic radicals, not ring substitution.

explanation: The mechanism of side-chain oxidation is complex and involves reaction of C–H bonds at the position next to the aromatic ring to form intermediate benzylic radicals. That's why a benzylic hydrogen is needed for the reaction.

prompt: Which alkylbenzene is NOT oxidized by KMnO4?

choices.text: tert-Butylbenzene
Toluene
choices.why: Toluene's methyl group has benzylic hydrogens, so it is oxidized to benzoic acid.

choices.text: Ethylbenzene
choices.why: Ethylbenzene has benzylic hydrogens on the carbon next to the ring, so it is oxidized.

choices.text: Butylbenzene
choices.why: Butylbenzene is the section's example: it is oxidized to benzoic acid in 85% yield.

explanation: Side-chain oxidation starts at C–H bonds on the carbon next to the ring. tert-Butylbenzene has no benzylic hydrogens, because its benzylic carbon is bonded to three methyl groups, so it is inert to KMnO4.

prompt: What aromatic product forms when p-tert-butyltoluene (1-tert-butyl-4-methylbenzene) is oxidized with KMnO4?

choices.text: p-tert-Butylbenzoic acid
Terephthalic acid
choices.why: Only the methyl group has benzylic hydrogens. The tert-butyl group has none, so it isn't oxidized.

choices.text: p-Methylbenzoic acid
choices.why: It's the other way around: the methyl group is oxidized, and the tert-butyl group, with no benzylic hydrogens, survives.

choices.text: No reaction, because the tert-butyl group protects the ring
choices.why: The methyl group still has benzylic hydrogens and is oxidized to –CO2H.

explanation: Exercise 16.8.1b: the methyl group has benzylic hydrogens and is oxidized to a carboxyl group, but the tert-butyl group has no benzylic hydrogens and is inert. The product is p-tert-butylbenzoic acid.

prompt: How is the neurotransmitter norepinephrine biosynthesized from dopamine?

choices.text: By benzylic hydroxylation through a radical mechanism, catalyzed by a copper enzyme
By electrophilic hydroxylation of the aromatic ring with an “OH+ equivalent”
choices.why: The OH goes on the side chain, at the benzylic position, not on the ring.

choices.text: By oxidation of the side chain to a carboxylic acid with KMnO4
choices.why: The enzyme adds an OH at the benzylic carbon; the side chain isn't cleaved to –CO2H.

choices.text: By a Friedel–Crafts alkylation with an organodiphosphate
choices.why: No new carbon–carbon bond forms. The reaction is a benzylic hydroxylation.

explanation: Analogous side-chain oxidations occur in biosynthesis. Norepinephrine is made from dopamine by a benzylic hydroxylation catalyzed by dopamine β-monooxygenase, a copper-containing enzyme. A copper–oxygen species first abstracts the pro-R benzylic hydrogen to give a radical, and a hydroxyl is then transferred from copper to carbon.

prompt: What is the product when propylbenzene reacts with N-bromosuccinimide (NBS) in the presence of benzoyl peroxide?

choices.text: (1-Bromopropyl)benzene, from bromination at the benzylic position
(3-Bromopropyl)benzene, from bromination at the end of the chain
choices.why: Bromination occurs exclusively at the benzylic position, next to the ring.

choices.text: A mixture of (1-bromopropyl)-, (2-bromopropyl)-, and (3-bromopropyl)benzene
choices.why: The reaction does not give a mixture; bromination occurs only at the benzylic position.

choices.text: o- and p-Bromopropylbenzene, from ring substitution
choices.why: NBS with a radical initiator brominates the side chain, not the ring.

explanation: Side-chain bromination at the benzylic position occurs when an alkylbenzene is treated with NBS. Propylbenzene gives (1-bromopropyl)benzene in 97% yield with benzoyl peroxide as a radical initiator. Bromination occurs exclusively next to the ring and does not give a mixture of products.

prompt: In the benzylic bromination of an alkylbenzene with NBS, what is the role of benzoyl peroxide?

choices.text: It is a radical initiator
It is a Lewis acid catalyst that polarizes Br2
choices.why: That's the role of FeBr3 in ring bromination. Benzoyl peroxide starts the radical chain.

choices.text: It oxidizes the side chain to a carboxylic acid
choices.why: Side-chain oxidation uses KMnO4. In NBS bromination, benzoyl peroxide only initiates the radical reaction.

choices.text: It supplies the bromine atom that ends up in the product
choices.why: The bromine comes from Br2, which is formed from NBS and HBr. Benzoyl peroxide just initiates the reaction.

explanation: Propylbenzene reacts with NBS in the presence of benzoyl peroxide, (PhCO2)2, as a radical initiator. The reaction is a radical chain: a benzylic hydrogen is abstracted, the benzylic radical reacts with Br2, and the Br· radical formed carries on the chain.

prompt: Why does NBS bromination of an alkylbenzene occur only at the benzylic position?

choices.text: The benzylic radical intermediate is stabilized by resonance with the ring
The benzylic carbocation intermediate is stabilized by the ring
choices.why: The reaction goes through a radical, not a carbocation; the benzylic radical is resonance-stabilized.

choices.text: Benzylic C–H bonds are the only ones bulky enough to react
choices.why: The selectivity is electronic: the benzylic radical is stabilized by resonance with the ring.

choices.text: NBS coordinates to the ring and delivers bromine to the nearest carbon
choices.why: The selectivity comes from the stability of the benzylic radical intermediate.

explanation: Reaction occurs exclusively at the benzylic position because the benzylic radical intermediate is stabilized by resonance. Figure 16.8.1 shows the benzyl radical stabilized by overlap of its p orbital with the ring π electron system. The mechanism is like that of allylic bromination of alkenes (Section 10.3).

prompt: According to the spin-density surface of the benzyl radical, besides the benzylic carbon, which ring carbons share the unpaired electron?

choices.text: The ortho and para carbons
The meta carbons
choices.why: The unpaired electron is delocalized to the ortho and para carbons, not the meta ones.

choices.text: All six ring carbons equally
choices.why: The spin density appears on the ortho and para carbons only.

choices.text: Only the ring carbon attached to the side chain
choices.why: The unpaired electron is shared by the ortho and para carbons of the ring.

explanation: The benzyl radical is resonance-stabilized by overlap of its p orbital with the ring's π system. The spin-density surface in Figure 16.8.1 shows that the unpaired electron is shared by the ortho and para carbons of the ring.

prompt: In the mechanism of benzylic bromination with NBS, where does the Br2 that reacts with the benzylic radical come from?

choices.text: It is produced by a concurrent reaction of HBr with NBS
It is added to the reaction mixture along with FeBr3
choices.why: No Br2 or FeBr3 is added. Br2 forms in small amounts when HBr reacts with NBS.

choices.text: It comes from the benzoyl peroxide initiator
choices.why: Benzoyl peroxide has no bromine; it only initiates the radical chain.

choices.text: It forms when two benzylic radicals combine
choices.why: Benzylic radicals have no bromine to release. Br2 comes from HBr reacting with NBS.

explanation: A benzylic hydrogen is abstracted to give a benzylic radical, which reacts with Br2 to give product and a Br· radical that carries on the chain. The Br2 needed is produced in step 3 by a concurrent reaction of HBr with NBS.

prompt: Which sequence would prepare styrene (C6H5CH=CH2) from benzene, using reactions you've studied?

choices.text: 1. CH3CH2Cl, AlCl3; 2. NBS; 3. KOH, ethanol
1. CH3CH2Cl, AlCl3; 2. KOH, ethanol; 3. NBS
choices.why: Ethylbenzene has no leaving group, so KOH can't cause elimination before the benzylic bromine is in place.

choices.text: 1. NBS; 2. CH3CH2Cl, AlCl3; 3. KOH, ethanol
choices.why: NBS brominates benzylic positions. Benzene has no side chain, so it must be alkylated first.

choices.text: 1. H2C=CHCl, AlCl3
choices.why: Vinylic halides don't react in Friedel–Crafts alkylations, because vinylic carbocations are too high in energy.

explanation: Exercise 16.8.3: Friedel–Crafts alkylation with CH3CH2Cl and AlCl3 gives ethylbenzene. NBS then brominates the benzylic position, and elimination of HBr with KOH in ethanol gives styrene.
